newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Recent IPOs dominate lacklustre Singapore bourse.
newsitem.headline: Recent IPOs dominate lacklustre Singapore bourse.

text.p: Recent listings enlivened an otherwise dull Singapore stock market on Thursday, dealers said.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index closed down just 0.79 points at 2,083.23 -- exactly where it was at lunch.
Dealers said gains in Singapore Telecom and car retailer Cycle & Carriage balanced falls in Singapore Press, drinks firm Fraser & Neave and maritime-based industrial group Keppel Corp.
"It is difficult to get clients interested. Volume is so low," said one dealer. Total turnover was 102.04 million shares.
Singapore Telecom rose 14 cents to Singapore $3.28 on rumours it's weighting in key regional indices may be increased.
A spokesman for the company said he knew of no reason for the rise, which was accomplished on 4.62 million shares.
Shipyard Labroy Marine, which listed two weeks ago, was the most active share with 11.08 million shares changing hands as it rose just two cents to S$1.20.
Dealers said almost all the volume was from retail clients.
The foreign shares of national carrier SIA fell another 20 cents to S$12.40 after some gloomy comments by its chief executive in a Reuters interview on Wednesday.
